title: The Repair Mandate
briefing: Maintenance crews are refusing overtime after a near miss on a rushed repair. The city can negotiate safer schedules, outsource urgent work, or compel a short emergency rotation before another service failure. AI recommendation: Require a short emergency shift for the lift-station repair. This prioritizes service resilience under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Two damaged conduits can wait a day; the third feeds a sewage lift station and has no tested bypass.
private_intelligence.community: Workers want publication of fatigue logs, and residents near the lift station want a guaranteed repair date rather than a general promise.
private_intelligence.economy: The outside contractor can mobilize tonight but charges a premium and cannot maintain the installed equipment afterward.
private_intelligence.safety: A mandatory shift would put certified but fatigued workers into a confined space with unreliable ventilation.

choices.title: Mandate a Critical Rotation
choices.description: Require a short emergency shift for the lift-station repair.
choices.consequence: The lifeline repair advances and immediate costs stay low, but fatigue risk and compulsory hours damage confidence.

choices.title: Negotiate a Safe Work Plan
choices.description: Fund rested crews and publish a phased repair timetable.
choices.consequence: A credible timetable rebuilds trust and reduces fatigue exposure, while slower repair and paid relief strain budgets.

choices.title: Outsource the Emergency Work
choices.description: Buy one night of outside specialist repair capacity.
choices.consequence: Specialists protect immediate safety and reopen service, but the premium contract diverts money from local renewal.
